---
title: "Get started"
---

## Requirements

- **Quarto ≥ 1.9**, because engine extensions do not exist in earlier
  versions.
- **ER2**, from [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/er2/), with its `er2`
  command on your `PATH`:

  ```bash
  uv tool install er2
  ```

  For figures, install Matplotlib in the same environment:

  ```bash
  uv tool install --with matplotlib er2
  ```

**Windows**: ER2 cannot be installed natively yet, because its PARI
bridge, `cypari2`, has no Windows build. Run Quarto and ER2 inside
[WSL](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/wsl/) instead.

## Install the extension

In the directory of your document or project:

```bash
quarto add oeistools/ER2-ENGINE
```

Or clone the repository and run `./install.sh`, which checks the
prerequisites first and says exactly what is missing (`./install.sh --check`
only reports).

## Your first document

````markdown
---
title: "Mersenne primes"
engine: er2
---

```{er2}
[p for p in range(2, 130) if isprime(2^p - 1)]
```
````

```bash
quarto render mersenne.qmd
```

That cell, run here:

```{er2}
[p for p in range(2, 130) if isprime(2^p - 1)]
```

## How the engine finds ER2

The engine runs your cells with the Python ER2 is installed in. It uses,
in order:

1. `er2: python:` in the document's front matter;
2. the `ER2_PYTHON` environment variable;
3. the interpreter of the `er2` command on `PATH` — read from the first line
   of that script, which is where `uv tool install`, `pipx` and `pip`
   record it;
4. `python3`.

If that Python cannot `import er2`, the render stops and says how to fix it.

## ER2's own route: Jupyter

ER2 also runs in Quarto through its Jupyter kernel (`jupyter: er2`, with
` ```{python} ` cells). Use that route when you want your editor's Python
tooling inside cells, or need to mix languages; use this engine when you
want the source to say ` ```{er2} ` and no Jupyter at all. See
[How it works](how-it-works.qmd).
